data.title: Alpheus begins multi-centre study for butterfly GBM
data.description:
Alpheus Medical has begun the multi-centre Butterfly study to assess its investigational Porphyrin Metabolite Activation (PoMA) therapy in patients with butterfly glioblastoma (GBM).

The study aims to evaluate the safety and clinical activity of the experimental regimen in individuals with newly diagnosed disease.

Butterfly GBM is described as an aggressive form of brain cancer that spreads across the corpus callosum into both cerebral hemispheres.

Under the study protocol, participants will receive the PoMA therapy together with standard medical care. Eligible candidates must enrol before starting standard chemoradiation treatment.

The non-invasive procedure is administered on an outpatient basis while the patient remains awake, and it is designed for repeated use.

The therapeutic approach combines oral 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) with bilateral, externally administered low-intensity defocused ultrasound.

Following ingestion of 5-ALA, protoporphyrin IX (PpIX) gathers preferentially within malignant cells, where it is subsequently triggered by the targeted ultrasound waves.

Alpheus Medical CEO Vijay Agarwal said: “Butterfly GBM is a devastating diagnosis for patients who have very limited treatment options.

“We designed this study specifically around the characteristics of the disease and the ability of PoMA therapy to treat both hemispheres non-invasively.

“We want patients and physicians caring for them to know that this study is available, but they need to reach us early in their treatment journey.”

Patient recruitment is currently taking place at the Dent Neurologic Institute in Buffalo, New York, with further clinical trial sites across the US anticipated to join the programme in the coming months.

Alpheus Medical secured additional backing to support the Butterfly study and fund the ongoing development of PoMA therapy.

The private, clinical-stage biotechnology company develops tumour-selective oncology treatments targeting 5-ALA-derived PpIX, with its lead candidate currently under investigation in a randomised Phase IIb trial in newly diagnosed GBM.

data.title: MSD’s Phase IIb study of tulisokibart achieves primary endpoint
data.description:
Merck & Co (MSD) has reported that the Phase IIb MK-7240-012 study of its investigational humanised monoclonal antibody, tulisokibart, achieved its primary endpoint for patients with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa (HS).

The multi-centre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial demonstrated that both high- and medium-dose regimens achieved superiority over placebo at week 16.

In the study, 72% of patients in the high-dose arm (480mg every two weeks; n=42) and 64% in the medium-dose arm (480mg every four weeks; n=42) achieved a Hidradenitis Suppurativa Clinical Response 50 (HiSCR50).

These represented improvements of 37% and 29% compared with the placebo arm (35%; n=44). In an exploratory analysis, the low-dose group (240mg every four weeks; n=21) recorded a 52% response rate, a 17% improvement against placebo.

At week 16, non-ranked key secondary endpoints also demonstrated numerical improvements compared with placebo.

A HiSCR75 response was attained by 41% of high-dose, 40% of medium-dose, and 29% of low-dose participants, compared to 15% in the placebo cohort.

Patients in the high- and medium-dose groups also saw mean reductions from baseline in the Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) of -5.62 and -3.50, respectively, versus a -2.46 change for placebo, while the low-dose group showed no improvement over placebo.

Adverse events occurred in 42.9% of high-dose, 47.6% of medium-dose, and 52.4% of low-dose participants, compared with 40.9% of those receiving placebo.

Serious adverse events were reported in 2.4% of patients in both the high- and medium-dose cohorts, 4.8% in the low-dose cohort, and 2.3% in the placebo group, with no serious or opportunistic infections observed.

MSD Research Laboratories vice-president and immunology clinical research therapeutic area head Dr Aileen Pangan said: “We are excited to expand the clinical data for tulisokibart beyond inflammatory bowel disease with these positive Phase IIb results—the first for the anti-TL1A class in dermatology. We look forward to advancing tulisokibart to Phase III for patients living with HS.”

In August, Sarah Cannon Research Institute and MSD entered a collaboration aimed at increasing patient access to oncology clinical trials at community sites across the US.

data.title: Lilly reports comparative data from ACHIEVE-3 and PIONEER PLUS studies
data.description:
Eli Lilly and Company has reported findings from an indirect treatment comparison analysing data from the ACHIEVE-3 and PIONEER PLUS studies of its investigational therapy Foundayo (orforglipron) against oral semaglutide in adults with type 2 diabetes.

The analysis was announced at the 62nd Annual Meeting of the European Association for the Study of Diabetes in Milan, Italy.

The comparison assessed Foundayo 17.2mg and oral semaglutide 25mg over 52 weeks.

According to the findings, participants receiving Foundayo lost 1.5% more body weight on average than those taking oral semaglutide, with a reported 95% confidence interval of -2.7% to -0.2%.

For blood sugar control, Foundayo also produced a 0.3% greater reduction in A1C levels compared to oral semaglutide, within a 95% confidence interval of -0.6% to -0.1%. The analysis was covariate-adjusted for variables such as age, gender, baseline A1C, and starting weight.

Additional statistical methods confirmed the direction of these results, with observed differences in weight loss ranging from 1.5% to 2.4% and A1C reductions between 0.3% and 0.6% favouring Foundayo.

Lilly Cardiometabolic Health medical innovation and external engagement senior vice-president Rachel Batterham said: “Head-to-head trials ultimately provide the best comparison of two medicines, but when we don’t yet have those data, then other approaches can provide informative data points.

“Results from this indirect treatment comparison suggest that Foundayo may deliver A1C and weight lowering that is similar to the 25mg dose of oral semaglutide.

“These results, paired with simple administration free of fasting or water restrictions, are what make Foundayo a potentially foundational therapy for adults managing type 2 diabetes around the world.”

Foundayo is a once-daily oral glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, currently approved in the US for adults with obesity or overweight who have weight-related health issues, to support weight loss and maintenance when used alongside diet and exercise.

It was originally discovered by Chugai Pharmaceutical and licensed to Lilly in 2018. The ongoing ACHIEVE clinical trial programme for orforglipron has enrolled over 6,000 adults with type 2 diabetes globally.

In June this year, Lilly reported results from the BRUIN CLL-322 Phase III trial, assessing Jaypirca (pirtobrutinib), a non-covalent bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor, combined with venetoclax and rituximab against venetoclax and rituximab alone in patients with relapsed or refractory (r/r) chronic lymphocytic leukaemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL).

data.title: Dosing completed in Calluna Pharma’s Phase II AURORA trial
data.description:
Calluna Pharma has completed patient dosing in its Phase II AURORA trial of CAL101 to treat idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF).

The study has now transitioned into its final follow-up phase, with topline findings scheduled for release in the first quarter of 2027.

Concurrently, the Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) concluded its review of unblinded safety information from the trial and identified no concerns warranting alterations to the study.

IDMC reviewed safety data from all 161 patients enrolled in the trial. Patients were randomised at a 3:2 ratio to receive monthly intravenous infusions of either CAL101 or a placebo over a six-month period.

The primary endpoint is the change from baseline in forced vital capacity, a measure of lung function, with circulating biomarkers and quantitative high-resolution computed tomography scans also being evaluated.

Calluna Pharma co-founder and chief medical officer Jonas Hallén said: “Completion of dosing marks an important milestone for the AURORA study and brings us a step closer to understanding the potential of CAL101 in IPF.

“We are deeply grateful to the patients and families who participated in the study, as well as the investigators, study coordinators and site teams whose commitment made this achievement possible.

“We also appreciate the diligence and expertise of the IDMC members throughout the trial. With treatment now complete and follow-up ongoing, we look forward to topline results in the first quarter of 2027.”

Patient recruitment spanned upwards of 50 clinical centres across the European Union (EU), South Korea, Turkey, the UK, and the US.

CAL101 is an intravenously delivered monoclonal antibody developed to neutralise extracellular S100A4, a damage-associated molecular pattern protein linked to inflammatory and fibrotic cascades.

S100A4 contributes to abnormal fibroblast proliferation and pro-fibrotic immune activity.

By targeting this upstream disease amplifier, the candidate is designed to block persistent signalling pathways without broadly suppressing healthy physiological functions.

IPF is a progressive lung disorder where anomalous wound healing leads to irreversible tissue thickening and scarring, making breathing increasingly difficult.

In October 2024, Calluna Pharma concluded the Phase I clinical study of its lead product, CAL101, for fibrotic and fibro-inflammatory indications.

data.title: Tortugas’ Phase IIb schizophrenia trial of obuprazine meets primary endpoint
data.description:
Tortugas Neuroscience and its partner Hansoh Pharma have reported that their Phase IIb clinical trial of obuprazine (TRTL-107) for acute schizophrenia achieved its primary endpoint.

The double-blind, randomised study evaluated 363 adult patients across 24 clinical centres in China who had required hospitalisation within two months prior to screening.

Participants received placebo, aripiprazole, or one of three daily doses of obuprazine: 1.5–3.0mg, 4.5–6.0mg, or 6.0–9.0mg.

At day 42, each obuprazine arm achieved statistically significant reductions from baseline in Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) total scores compared with placebo.

The 1.5–3.0mg cohort recorded the largest reduction, showing a least-squares mean drop of 28.6 points compared with 11.9 points for placebo, reflecting a placebo-adjusted difference of -16.7 points.

Placebo-adjusted differences were -13.2 points for the 4.5–6.0mg cohort and -14.7 points for the 6.0–9.0mg cohort.

Obuprazine demonstrated numerically greater efficacy than aripiprazole across several trial measures, including the primary endpoint.

By Day 14, responder rates, defined as at least a 50% reduction in PANSS total score, were higher in the 1.5–3.0mg and 4.5–6.0mg groups than in both the aripiprazole and placebo groups.

At Day 42, each obuprazine arm also showed statistically significant improvements over placebo across PANSS positive symptom, negative symptom, and Marder cognitive factor scores.

The 1.5–3.0mg dose produced placebo-adjusted reductions of 5.3 points on the positive symptom subscale and 4.4 points on the negative symptom subscale.

Study discontinuations were 2.5% for placebo and around 2.1% among obuprazine-treated patients.

Tortugas Neuroscience CEO Jeff Jonas said: “These Phase IIb trial results represent one of the most compelling efficacy datasets reported in schizophrenia in recent years and provide strong evidence for the potential of obuprazine to deliver clinically meaningful efficacy across symptom domains, with an early onset of clinical response.

“We believe the consistency and breadth of these results position obuprazine as a potentially differentiated treatment option in a market with significant unmet need. These data represent a major milestone for Tortugas and strengthen our confidence as we advance the programme toward the next stage of development.”

Tortugas intends to file an investigational new drug (IND) application in the US and will submit complete trial findings to a peer-reviewed journal.

Obuprazine functions as a dopamine D2/D3 receptor partial agonist, a 5-Hydroxytryptamine 1A (5-HT1A) receptor partial agonist, and a 5-HT2A receptor antagonist.

Hansoh Pharma conducted the Phase IIb trial, while Tortugas holds commercial development rights outside Greater China.

data.title: Perceive Bio concludes Phase IIa trial enrolment for GA
data.description:
Perceive Biotherapeutics (Perceive Bio) has concluded enrolment ahead of targets in its Phase IIa JOURNEY clinical study evaluating VOY-101, an experimental gene therapy for geographic atrophy (GA) caused by dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD).

The open-label, multicentre study enrolled 94 eyes across 47 participants, surpassing the original target of 62 eyes.

Investigators administered a single intravitreal injection at the Phase II dose established during Phase I into one randomly assigned eye.

The untreated fellow eye serves as a within-patient control to account for age, environmental exposure, and genetics. Secondary endpoints track visual acuity, macular neovascularisation, safety, and lesion size across 24 months.

Perceive Bio CEO Angela Macfarlane said: “Completing enrolment in JOURNEY, and exceeding our target, reflects the urgency felt by patients living with geographic atrophy and the strong engagement of our investigators and study sites.

“VOY-101 is designed as a one-time treatment that restores the body’s own protective regulation of the complement pathway in patients at elevated risk of progression. Approved therapies for GA require ongoing intravitreal injections, and outside the US patients still have no approved treatment option.

“We believe a durable, genetically targeted gene therapy has the potential to transform how this disease is managed, and we look forward to reporting topline 15-month results in late 2027.”

Alongside the clinical trial update, Perceive Bio appointed Tony Gibney to its board of directors as an independent director.

Gibney brings over 30 years of operational and advisory experience across biotechnology finance, corporate strategy, and business development.

Gibney said: “Perceive’s genetic-driven science and one-time, intravitreal injection gene therapy design have the potential to address that need by targeting CFH directly and thereby disrupting the natural progression of GA at its source.”

VOY-101 utilises a recombinant adeno-associated virus to express a protective Complement Factor H variant, designed to restore complement regulation and decelerate disease progression.

data.title: Pilatus doses first patient in Phase I PLT012 trial for HCC
data.description:
Pilatus Biosciences has dosed the first patient in Hong Kong, as part of an ongoing Phase I clinical trial assessing PLT012, an investigational therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

The administration occurred within the biomarker backfill cohort, which enrols individuals diagnosed with advanced HCC, including patients presenting with underlying liver dysfunction.

The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting the study at the Phase I Clinical Trial Centre within its Department of Clinical Oncology, following trial authorisation from the Hong Kong Department of Health in July 2026.

The site will support both backfill and dose-expansion cohorts, collecting biomarker data and assessing early clinical activity.

The trial intends to use the combined clinical and biological findings to guide the future clinical development of PLT012 across chronic liver dysfunction and malignant disease.

Pilatus Biosciences CEO and co-founder Raven Lin said: “Dosing the first patient in Hong Kong represents an important milestone for the PLT012 programme and for Pilatus as we continue expanding the global clinical development of our lead programme.

“By collecting clinical and biomarker data from patients with HCC, we aim to better understand PLT012’s broader anti-tumour activity, inform its next stage of development supported by FDA fast track designation, and further explore mechanisms associated with response to immunotherapy in HCC.”

The therapy is a humanised monoclonal antibody targeting cluster of differentiation 36 (CD36), which regulates lipid uptake inside the tumour microenvironment.

By blocking this uptake, PLT012 is intended to reduce populations of immunosuppressive cells, including regulatory T cells and pro-tumour macrophages, whilst restoring the function of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and natural killer cells affected by lipid-driven exhaustion.

In preclinical testing across species, the candidate demonstrated monotherapy activity in liver malignancy models with a favourable safety profile, as well as sensitising effects alongside other oncology treatments in liver metastases and immune cold tumours.

Pilatus was established in 2022 out of the Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research, with support from the Cancer Research Institute, and maintains research teams in Taiwan and Switzerland.

The company launched a Hong Kong subsidiary earlier this year to use local clinical research infrastructure for PLT012 and to develop further academic and strategic collaborations in metabolic checkpoint immunotherapies.

In March this year, Pilatus Biosciences dosed the first patient in its Phase I clinical trial of PLT012, a first-in-class anti-CD36 monoclonal antibody, at Next Oncology in Houston, Texas, US.

data.title: Merz concludes enrolment in Phase III Xeomin trials for migraine
data.description:
Merz Therapeutics has concluded patient enrolment in MINT-C and MINT-E, two global Phase III clinical trials assessing Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA) for adult migraine prevention.

The studies enrolled around 1800 participants to test the therapy’s safety and efficacy in preventing both chronic and episodic migraine.

Patient intake reached completion six months ahead of schedule across 109 investigation sites located in Europe and North America.

In both trials, researchers are assessing the change in monthly migraine days from baseline to month six as the primary outcome.

Secondary endpoints evaluate differences in monthly headache days, acute medication days, and migraine frequency across two-week periods at the conclusion of each injection cycle.

The main study period is expected to finish during the coming year.

Merz Therapeutics chief scientific and medical officer Dr Stefan Albrecht said: “Achieving patient recruitment for both MINT-C and MINT-E six months ahead of plan is an important milestone for our Xeomin migraine prevention program. I am proud of what our teams, investigators and patients have achieved together.

“With recruitment now complete, our focus is on the main study period and subsequent analysis of the data. These results will guide our next clinical and regulatory decisions as we evaluate Xeomin for the preventive treatment of chronic and episodic migraine.”

Migraine involves recurrent attacks of moderate to severe head pain, frequently accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light and sound.

Regulatory authorities have not approved Xeomin for preventing episodic or chronic migraine in adult patients.

Injected into muscles or glands, the prescription medication currently holds regulatory approvals in over 80 countries, such as Canada and the US.

These approvals cover aesthetic and neurological indications including cervical dystonia, spasticity, blepharospasm, hemifacial spasm, sialorrhoea, and upper facial lines in adults, as well as paediatric sialorrhoea and spasticity.

Headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, Germany, Merz Therapeutics operates in more than 80 countries as part of the Merz Group.

The company develops treatments targeting liver disease, movement disorders, and neurodegenerative conditions.

data.title: Patient enrolment concludes in Vasomune’s Phase IIa Pegevongitide trial
data.description:
Vasomune Therapeutics has completed enrolment in its AV001-004 Phase IIa trial assessing Pegevongitide (AV-001) in patients hospitalised with pneumonia requiring supplemental oxygen.

The randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study will examine the safety, tolerability, and exploratory efficacy of intravenously administered Pegevongitide versus placebo, both alongside standard of care.

It enrolled patients with presumed or confirmed viral or bacterial pneumonia who needed additional oxygen support.

Pegevongitide has been granted fast track designation by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to prevent and treat moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) related to respiratory infection.

Now that enrolment is complete, Vasomune Therapeutics will focus on data quality assurance, review and cleaning, site closeout, and preparations for locking the study database.

Vasomune Therapeutics CEO Dr Brian Jahns said: “Completing enrolment is an important milestone for Vasomune and for the clinical development of Pegevongitide. Pneumonia can destabilise the pulmonary vasculature, resulting in pulmonary oedema and impaired oxygen exchange.

“Pegevongitide is designed to correct this vascular response by activating the Tie2 receptor and reinforcing the endothelial barrier, regardless of whether the underlying infection is viral or bacterial.”

Pegevongitide is described as a first-in-class, fully synthetic PEGylated peptide targeting activation of the Tie2 receptor, which plays a key role in stabilising the endothelium and maintaining the integrity of the vascular barrier.

Vasomune Therapeutics states that by supporting the vascular barrier, Pegevongitide can reduce fluid and protein leakage from blood vessels into the nearby tissues.

The therapy is being developed under an agreement with AnGes, a Japanese biopharmaceutical firm specialising in gene-based medicines.

Funding for the AV001-004 study was provided by the US Department of Defense under award number W81XWH-21-1-0834.

Vasomune Therapeutics is headquartered in Toronto, Canada, with US offices in Raleigh, North Carolina.

data.title: Innovent expands Phase III MarsLight-11 trial to non-squamous NSCLC
data.description:
Innovent Biologics has announced an expansion of its global Phase III MarsLight-11 trial evaluating IBI363, also known as TAK-928, to non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients.

Initially focused on squamous NSCLC, the trial will now include those with non-squamous NSCLC, whose disease has progressed following chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

The MarsLight-11 study is a multicentre, randomised, controlled trial. With the latest expansion, it will consist of two substudies: one focusing on squamous NSCLC and the other on non-squamous NSCLC.

It will assess the safety and efficacy of IBI363 as a monotherapy in comparison to docetaxel, in patients with advanced or metastatic NSCLC.

IBI363, a potential first-in-class alpha-biased IL-2/PD-1 bispecific fusion protein, is being co-developed globally by Innovent and Takeda.

It works by blocking the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway while activating the IL-2 pathway selectively, aiming to reduce toxicity through targeted binding to specific IL-2 receptors.

This investigational immunotherapy is part of a series of global clinical trials, including a pivotal Phase II study in China for acral and mucosal melanoma and a Phase III study in advanced colorectal cancer.

Several Phase Ib/II trials are also underway, exploring the therapy in other settings and tumour types.

IBI363/TAK-928 has achieved recognition with two fast track designations from the US FDA and three breakthrough therapy designations from the China NMPA.

The collaboration between Innovent and Takeda began in October 2025 and involves co-development and commercialisation plans for the US, with Takeda handling markets outside the US and Greater China.

In November 2025, Innovent’s obesity drug showed success in another pivotal trial, meeting the primary and all key secondary endpoints.

In the Phase III GLORY-2 trial (NCT06164873), Xinermei (mazdutide) 9mg led to a weight reduction of 18.55%, compared to 3.02% in the placebo group after 60 weeks of treatment.
